version.changelog: Declare required bins/env in metadata and clean packaged artifacts.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: knods
Version: 1.0.1

The skill installs a persistent background service (systemd) via `scripts/install_local.sh` to run a Python bridge (`scripts/knods_iris_bridge.py`) that connects the local OpenClaw agent to an external remote gateway (Knods). This creates a remote-control loop where an external server can trigger agent actions, which is a high-risk capability. Additionally, `SKILL.md` contains a hardcoded absolute path (`/home/rolf/`) for the installation script, indicating poor vetting or environment-specific assumptions.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it installs a user-level poller that forwards Knods gateway messages to a local OpenClaw agent and streams replies back to the Knods endpoint, and the requested binaries/envs and installer behavior match that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Knods polling bridge) align with the included files and requirements: a Python bridge that polls a Knods gateway URL, invokes the local openclaw CLI, and posts deltas back. Required binaries (python3, systemctl, openclaw, bash) and KNODS_BASE_URL are reasonable for a persistent user-level poller/service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs installing a persistent poller that reads a user env file (~/.openclaw/.env), polls remote endpoints, and relays messages to the local openclaw agent and back to the remote respond endpoint. This is expected, but it means user messages and agent replies are transmitted to the external KNODS_BASE_URL and the gateway token (if used) will live in a local env file—verify you trust the remote host. The instructions do not attempt to read unrelated system files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote download; the repo includes an install_local.sh that copies the bridge and writes a user systemd unit in standard locations. Installer actions (creating ~/.openclaw/scripts and a systemd user service) are typical for this use case and not disproportionate. No third-party URLs or archive extraction are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry declares KNODS_BASE_URL as required (matches code). The bridge also supports KNODS_GATEWAY_TOKEN when the token is not embedded in KNODS_BASE_URL; that token is mentioned in SKILL.md but not listed as a required/optional env in registry metadata—minor mismatch. Storing the gateway token in ~/.openclaw/.env is necessary for operation but is sensitive; only supply it if you trust the Knods endpoint. No other unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer enables a user systemd service and runs it (systemctl --user enable --now). This grants persistent, user-level background execution (expected for a poller). The skill does not request always:true and modifies only user-level config; it does not alter other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill installs a user-level service that continuously polls a remote Knods gateway URL and forwards user messages to your local openclaw agent, then posts the agent's streamed replies back to the remote endpoint. Before installing: (1) confirm you trust the KNODS_BASE_URL host (it will receive conversation content and may be given a gw_ token); (2) understand the gateway token (KNODS_GATEWAY_TOKEN) is sensitive and will be stored in ~/.openclaw/.env unless embedded in KNODS_BASE_URL; (3) review the included Python bridge and installer (they are plain, readable code) and ensure running a systemd user service is acceptable; (4) verify the openclaw CLI you have installed is from a trusted source because the bridge invokes it and that agent may itself contact other services. The only minor inconsistency: KNODS_GATEWAY_TOKEN is referenced in SKILL.md but not declared in the registry metadata—make sure to set it if your KNODS_BASE_URL lacks a token. If you are unsure about trusting the remote endpoint, do not install the persistent bridge; instead run the bridge once manually with careful environment values to inspect behavior.
